new.title: Meet sharks and penguins at Océanopolis
new.desc: Océanopolis opened in 1990 as the Maison de la Mer, and two pavilions, polar and tropical, were added in 2000. It holds about 4 million litres of seawater, 1 million of them in the shark aquarium.
new.tip: Allow half a day and check seasonal hours on oceanopolis.com. Bus line 3 serves the marina stop.
new.q: Océanopolis, Port de Plaisance du Moulin Blanc, Brest

new.title: Tour the Château de Brest and its naval museum
new.desc: The fortress guarding the Penfeld harbour mouth houses the Musée national de la Marine, with ship models, navigation instruments and paintings on the history of the navy and the Brest arsenal. The castle also hosts the maritime prefecture.
new.tip: Closed for the annual break in January; last admission is 17:30. The ramparts give views over the harbour.
new.q: Château de Brest, Boulevard de la Marine, Brest

new.title: Cross the Pont de Recouvrance lift bridge
new.desc: Opened on 17 July 1954, this vertical-lift bridge over the Penfeld has 70 m towers and an 88 m span weighing 525 tonnes. It was Europe's largest vertical-lift bridge until 2008 and lifts roughly fifty times a year.
new.tip: Walk across for views of the Penfeld; lifts are announced locally and take about fifteen minutes.

new.title: Wander the Ateliers des Capucins
new.desc: The former naval arsenal workshops on the Penfeld's right bank reopened to the public in 2016 as a cultural and leisure district. It is reached by an urban cable car from the centre.
new.tip: Free to walk around; it is at 25 rue de Pontaniou. Combine with a drink or a stop at the Penfeld viewpoints.
new.q: Ateliers des Capucins, 25 rue de Pontaniou, Brest

new.title: Climb into the Tour Tanguy history museum
new.desc: This 14th-century tower on a rock above the Penfeld in Recouvrance houses the Musée du Vieux Brest. Fourteen dioramas by Jim-E. Sévellec retrace the city's events and daily life, and the city took over the tower in 1954.
new.tip: The tower was refurbished in 2023 and has an audioguide; confirm current hours and price before you go.

new.title: Stroll the Jardin des explorateurs
new.desc: A free garden in the Batterie du Cavalier, inaugurated on 20 March 2002, planted with species brought back by explorers and botanists who sailed from Brest. A belvedere looks over the château, the harbour and the naval base.
new.tip: Entrance is on rue de la Pointe; hours vary by season, so check before going. Tram line A stops at Recouvrance.
new.q: Jardin des explorateurs, rue de la Pointe, Recouvrance, Brest

new.title: Walk Rue Saint-Malo, Brest's oldest street
new.desc: Only the lower stretch of this cobbled lane in Recouvrance survived the 1944 bombing, about 94 m of 17th and 18th century houses. The association Vivre la Rue, founded in 1989, keeps the street alive with events.
new.tip: Pedestrian and free; best in daylight when the craft shops and cafés are open.

new.title: Explore the Conservatoire botanique in Stang-Alar
new.desc: Founded in 1975 as the first institution of its kind, the Conservatoire botanique national de Brest has its garden in the Stang-Alar valley, a former quarry. Threatened plants grow beside tropical greenhouses over roughly 30 hectares.
new.tip: Address is 39 allée du Bot; check opening times on cbnbrest.fr.
new.q: Conservatoire botanique national de Brest, 39 allée du Bot, Brest

new.title: Watch the harbour from the Cours Dajot
new.desc: A public promenade of nearly 500 m under plane trees, rising about 30 m above the commercial port and the roadstead. The US naval monument, known as the Tour Rose, stands in its centre.
new.tip: Open at any hour and free; sunset over the rade is the best moment.

new.title: Order a kig ha farz at Au P'ty Lyonnais
new.desc: This restaurant near the Halles Saint-Louis serves kig ha farz, the North Finistère meat-and-buckwheat-pudding stew, as a regular dish. Brest Métropole Tourisme highlights it among local addresses.
new.tip: Open Wednesday to Saturday lunch and dinner and Sunday lunch; book at weekends.
new.q: Au P'ty Lyonnais, rue de Lyon, Brest

new.title: Eat a galette at Crêperie Moderne
new.desc: Founded in 1922 and run by the Boënnec family for four generations, this crêperie on rue d'Algésiras is one of Brest's oldest. Reviewers single out the sausage gratin crêpe.
new.tip: Pair with Breton cider; try the saucisse galette.

new.title: Have crêpes by the Recouvrance quay at Latitude Crêpe
new.desc: A crêperie on the Quai de la Douane open since 2004, with a terrace facing the schooner La Recouvrance. It is rated 4.4 across 54 reviews on one guide.
new.tip: Book on summer evenings; the terrace faces the quay.
new.q: Latitude Crêpe, Quai de la Douane, Brest

new.title: Taste craft beer at En Bières Inconnues
new.desc: A beer cellar in the Ateliers des Capucins that brews its own six beers, some fruit-flavoured, and sells brews from Brittany and around the world. Tastings are possible on site.
new.tip: Open 10:00 to 19:00, closed Monday; it also runs brewing workshops.
new.q: En Bières Inconnues, 25 rue de Pontaniou, Brest

new.title: Try Molène sausage at Crêperie de Cornouaille
new.desc: A buttery crêperie on rue Saint-Marc, listed by Brest Métropole Tourisme, with Molène sausage among its fillings. Reviewers praise the crisp, generously filled galettes.
new.tip: Order the galette saucisse de Molène with cider.
new.q: Crêperie de Cornouaille, rue Saint-Marc, Brest

new.title: Swim at Plage du Moulin Blanc
new.desc: Brest's main beach is about 800 m long next to the marina and the Stang-Alar park. It is supervised in season, with parking, showers and toilets, and calm shallow water.
new.tip: Bring a towel for summer afternoons; the marina cafés are a short walk.

new.title: Visit the Brasserie Poèm brewery
new.desc: An organic craft brewery at 490 rue Alain Colas, near the marina. It offers 30 to 45 minute tours ending with a tasting at the bar, with summer openings.
new.tip: Check tour dates and booking on the brewery's page.
new.q: Brasserie Poèm, 490 rue Alain Colas, Brest

new.title: Cruise the Rade de Brest by boat
new.desc: Boat trips leave the commercial harbour past the naval base and the Portzic lighthouse and cross the goulet. Operators include Le Febvre Prestations Maritimes and traditional sailing vessels such as Notre Dame de Rumengol.
new.tip: Check operators for dates; most sail April to September.

new.title: Browse the Saint-Louis market
new.desc: The largest market in Brest spreads over rue de Lyon, the Halles and the church car park. The covered halls were destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt in their present form.
new.tip: Go in the morning; the halls were being refurbished, so stalls may be outside.
new.q: Halles Saint-Louis, rue de Lyon, Brest

new.title: Ride the Brest cable car over the Penfeld
new.desc: France's first urban cable car dedicated to everyday transport opened in November 2016 and links the centre to the Capucins in about 3 minutes. A normal tram or bus ticket works on it.
new.tip: Service has had interruptions, so check status; tickets are valid for one hour of transfers.

new.title: Climb the Pointe Saint-Mathieu lighthouse
new.desc: The headland at Plougonvelin holds a lighthouse built in 1835, the ruins of the Abbaye Saint-Mathieu de Fine-Terre and a signal station. Visitors can climb 163 steps to the gallery.
new.tip: Lighthouse hours vary, so check the tourism listing; arrive for sunset over the Iroise.
new.q: Pointe Saint-Mathieu, 3 rue des Moines, Plougonvelin

new.title: Visit the Créac'h lighthouse museum on Ouessant
new.desc: The Musée des Phares et Balises sits in the former power station of the Créac'h lighthouse, one of the world's most powerful with a range of 61 km. It holds Fresnel lenses and signalling equipment.
new.tip: Check the Parc naturel régional d'Armorique site for opening hours; rent a bike on the island.
new.q: Phare du Créac'h, Musée des Phares et Balises, Ouessant

new.title: See the Lagatjar standing stones near Pen-Hir
new.desc: The alignments of Lagatjar are rows of megaliths listed as historic monument as early as 1883, close to the Pointe de Pen-Hir road. They are free to visit.
new.tip: Park near the stones and walk 10 to 15 minutes on to the headland.

new.title: Visit the Tour Vauban and boat graveyard at Camaret
new.desc: The polygonal Tour Vauban on the Sillon is part of the defences of the goulet de Brest and a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2008. A boat graveyard lies beside it.
new.tip: Walk the Sillon at low tide light for the wrecks; the tower interior has set hours.

new.title: Wander Locronan around the Église Saint-Ronan
new.desc: Locronan is a Petite Cité de Caractère and one of the Plus beaux villages de France, centred on the granite houses of Place de l'Église. The Église Saint-Ronan and the Chapelle du Pénity hold the saint's tomb.
new.tip: Visit early or late to avoid the crowds; the village is free to walk.

new.title: Step aboard at the Port-Musée in Douarnenez
new.desc: The Port-Musée occupies an old cannery on the Port-Rhu with over 2,800 m² of exhibitions plus heritage boats afloat. One ticket covers the quayside museum and the boats.
new.tip: Boats afloat close from December to March; place de l'Enfer.

new.title: Stand on the Pointe du Raz
new.desc: The Pointe du Raz is a cliff about 72 m high on the Cap Sizun, a Grand Site de France with the Baie des Trépassés and Pointe du Van. From the path you see the Raz de Sein, the Vieille lighthouse and the Île de Sein.
new.tip: Parking at the point is paid; start at the Baie des Trépassés to avoid it.

new.title: Admire Quimper's Cathédrale Saint-Corentin
new.desc: Construction of this Gothic cathedral was decided in 1239 under Bishop Rainaud on the site of an 11th century church, and it became a minor basilica in 1870. It stands on Place Toul-al-Laër.
new.tip: Free entry; visit with a stroll along the Odet.

new.title: Discover Quimper faïence at the Musée de la Faïence
new.desc: Founded in 1991 by Bernard Verlingue, this private museum at 14 rue Jean-Baptiste Bousquet in Locmaria shows about 5,000 pieces over eight rooms. The HB-Henriot factory nearby offers tours.
new.tip: Factory workshop tours run April to September; the shop is open year-round.
new.q: Musée de la Faïence, 14 rue Jean-Baptiste Bousquet, Quimper

new.title: Follow Gauguin at the Musée de Pont-Aven
new.desc: Reopened on 26 March 2016 in the restored annex of the Hôtel Julia, the museum holds works by Gauguin, Émile Bernard, Sérusier and Maurice Denis. It also holds about 4,500 to 5,000 pieces tracing the Pont-Aven School.
new.tip: Pair it with the Bois d'Amour walk.
new.q: Musée de Pont-Aven, Place Julia, Pont-Aven

new.title: Walk the ramparts of the Ville Close
new.desc: The Ville Close is a fortified islet 350 m long and 100 m wide in Concarneau harbour, with ramparts classified in 1899 and modified by Vauban. A walkway runs along the walls.
new.tip: Cross the footbridge; the Musée de la Pêche is inside the walls.

new.title: Climb the Phare d'Eckmühl at Penmarc'h
new.desc: The lighthouse is 65 m tall, inaugurated in 1897 in memory of the Prince d'Eckmühl and funded by his daughter. Its beam reaches up to 45 km and visitors can climb 290 steps.
new.tip: Combine with the wave-lashed Saint-Guénolé rocks along the GR34.

new.title: Enter the Cairn de Barnenez
new.desc: Standing on the Kernéléhen peninsula at Plouézoc'h, this megalithic monument is described as a burial chamber older than the Pyramids. Entry is about 7 euros and a self-guided leaflet is available.
new.tip: Allow 1.5 hours; the promontory is windy.

new.title: See the parish close of Saint-Thégonnec
new.desc: The enclos combines a church, triumphal arch, wall, ossuary built between 1676 and 1682 and a calvary dated 1610. It is part of the Finistère parish closes UNESCO candidacy.
new.tip: Outside access is free.

new.title: Read the stone Bible at Guimiliau calvary
new.desc: The calvary of 1581 to 1588 shows dozens of figures in 16th century dress across more than 25 scenes of Christ's life. The church porch dates from 1606 to 1617.
new.tip: Entering the enclos is free; CIAP interpretation centre at 53 rue du Calvaire.

new.title: Climb the Kreisker bell tower in Saint-Pol-de-Léon
new.desc: The 14th and 15th century Kreisker chapel has a spire about 78 m high, among the tallest in Brittany. A spiral staircase of around 169 steps leads up.
new.tip: The cathedral of Paul Aurélien stands nearby.

new.title: Walk under the Morlaix viaduct
new.desc: The viaduct is about 292 m long and 62 m high and crosses the historic centre, built from 1861 to 1863 and registered in 1975. Its pedestrian level is reached by narrow alleys.
new.tip: Start from Maison Penanault on place Charles-de-Gaulle.

new.title: Eat scallop galettes at Crêperie du Frugy
new.desc: A well-regarded crêperie at 9 rue Sainte-Thérèse a few steps from the cathedral, founded in 2014. Reviewers recommend the scallop galette.
new.tip: Small room; book ahead.
new.q: Crêperie du Frugy, 9 rue Sainte-Thérèse, Quimper

new.title: Taste galettes de Pont-Aven at Traou Mad
new.desc: The Traou Mad biscuit factory was created in Pont-Aven by baker Alexis Le Villain in 1920. The factory shop sells galettes fines, palets bretons and caramels.
new.tip: Open every day; the town-centre shop faces the tourist office.
new.q: Biscuiterie Traou Mad, ZA de Kergazuel, Pont-Aven

new.title: Dine on Audierne langoustine at Le Goyen
new.desc: Le Goyen is a quayside hotel-restaurant in Audierne rated 13/20 by Gault&Millau, with langoustine tartare and Audierne lobster on the menu.
new.tip: Budget about 49 to 89 euros.
new.q: Le Goyen, Place Jean Simon, Audierne

new.title: Buy a kouign-amann at Boulangerie des Plomarc'h
new.desc: Douarnenez is credited as the birthplace of kouign-amann and Boulangerie des Plomarc'h at 20 rue des Plomarc'h is its top recommendation, run by Thierry Lucas.
new.tip: Buy early before they sell out.
new.q: Boulangerie des Plomarc'h, 20 rue des Plomarc'h, Douarnenez

new.title: Try an onion galette at Crêperie Ti Saozon
new.desc: At 30 rue Gambetta, Gault&Millau praises its organic Roscoff cider and rustic complètes, including one with andouille and Oignon Rosé de Roscoff.
new.tip: Try the Guémené galette.
new.q: Crêperie Ti Saozon, 30 rue Gambetta, Roscoff

new.title: Order buckwheat galettes at Le Pennti
new.desc: In the heart of the Ville Close, Le Pennti is renowned for crispy buckwheat pancakes and filled sweet crêpes, with a small inner courtyard.
new.tip: Galettes cost about 6 to 10 euros.

new.title: Taste tinned fish at Conserverie Kerbriant
new.desc: A small family cannery whose visit ends with a tasting of tuna and sardine specialities like white tuna velouté, fish rillettes and seaweed tartare.
new.tip: Visits last about 45 minutes; confirm the schedule.
new.q: Conserverie Kerbriant, 32 rue Jean Kervoalen, Parc d'Activités de Lannugat Nord, Douarnenez

new.title: Eat galettes at Atipik Bilig in Morlaix
new.desc: Founded in 2010 in the historic quarter, this crêperie serves galettes and crêpes plus tartines and salads.
new.tip: Crêperie Ty Bihan is a nearby alternative.

new.title: Eat Breton lobster at La Tatanerie in Camaret
new.desc: At 25 quai Gustave Toudouze, La Tatanerie is a waterfront restaurant known for homard breton, grilled or split and served simply.
new.tip: Check lobster availability and book.
new.q: La Tatanerie, 25 quai Gustave Toudouze, Camaret-sur-Mer

new.title: Try Molène sausage at Crêperie Ty Coz
new.desc: On Place de l'Église in Locronan, founded in 1952, known for buckwheat pancakes with smoked sausage from the Île de Molène.
new.tip: Sit near the square.
new.q: Crêperie Ty Coz, Place de l'Église, Locronan

new.title: Dine at L'Insolite in Douarnenez
new.desc: L'Insolite at the Hôtel de France, 4 rue Jean Jaurès, is Gault&Millau's chef's restaurant for Douarnenez, scored 13.5/20.
new.tip: Check the Brittany tourism "sea to plate" trip.

new.title: Try modern seafood at Orizhon in Audierne
new.desc: Orizhon at 2 quai Jacques-de-Thézac is listed by Michelin as modern seafood, with a terrace over the port and marina.
new.tip: Prices in the € bracket; book.

new.title: Eat mussels at Le Styvel in Camaret
new.desc: At 2 quai du Styvel, the restaurant curves along the harbour with views to the Tour Vauban. Reviewers praise the mussels.
new.tip: Choose a table by the window.
new.q: Le Styvel, 2 quai du Styvel, Camaret-sur-Mer

new.title: Sail from Le Conquet to Ouessant or Molène
new.desc: Penn ar Bed runs ferries from Le Conquet to Ouessant (about 1h15) and Molène (about 30 to 40 minutes) every day of the year. Some sailings to Ouessant stop at Molène.
new.tip: Check pennarbed.fr for timetables; tickets 02 98 80 80 80.
new.q: Embarcadère de Le Conquet, Le Conquet

new.title: Take the boat from Audierne to the Île de Sein
new.desc: Penn ar Bed runs a daily year-round service from Audierne Sainte-Évette, about 50 minutes to an hour. Cars and bikes are not allowed on the island.
new.tip: Outside summer, usually one round trip a day.

new.title: Sail to the Îles de Glénan
new.desc: Boats reach Saint-Nicolas, the main island, in about an hour from Bénodet, Concarneau, Loctudy and Fouesnant from April to September. Fares were about 39 euros return in 2024 to 2025.
new.tip: Bring swimwear and a picnic.

new.title: Ferry to the Île de Batz and its Delaselle garden
new.desc: The 15 minute vedette from Roscoff reaches Batz; the Jardin Georges Delaselle holds more than 2,500 species, bought in 1997 by the Conservatoire du littoral.
new.tip: Fare about 11 euros return; garden open April to September.
new.q: Jardin Georges Delaselle, Penn Batz, Île-de-Batz

new.title: Cruise the Morgat sea caves
new.desc: The Vedettes Sirènes sail from Quai Kador for a circuit of about 50 minutes into the caves, including the Souffleur and the Cheminées du Diable.
new.tip: Trips depend on weather and tide.

new.title: Cruise the Odet from Bénodet to Quimper
new.desc: The Vedettes de l'Odet run guided cruises up the river from Bénodet toward Quimper, with about 2h30 of sailing return depending on tides; a one-hour option exists.
new.tip: Open April to September.
new.q: Vedettes de l'Odet, 2 avenue de l'Odet, Vieux Port, Bénodet

new.title: Walk the GR34 to the Cap de la Chèvre
new.desc: The path at the cape follows the GR34 sentier des douaniers. A 7 km loop starts from the semaphore; the Morgat to cape stretch is about 13 km.
new.tip: Spring is best for gorse and wildflowers.

new.title: Hike from the Baie des Trépassés to the Pointe du Raz
new.desc: The coastal GR34 links the bay, popular with surfers, to the Pointe du Raz in a few kilometres, passing blockhouses.
new.tip: Starting at the bay avoids the paid parking.

new.title: Hike up the Roc'h Trévézel
new.desc: The Roc'h Trévézel reaches 385 m. A loop of about 3.6 km from the col de Trévézel climbs about 90 m, 1h15.
new.tip: Parts are unmarked; go in dry weather.
new.q: Col de Trévézel, Monts d'Arrée, Plounéour-Ménez

new.title: Wander the Huelgoat forest rock chaos
new.desc: The forest is known for granite boulders, the Roche Tremblante weighing over 100 tonnes, and the Gouffre where the Argent river drops about 8 m.
new.tip: Free; wear grippy shoes.

new.title: Watch the fish auction at Haliotika
new.desc: Haliotika in Le Guilvinec reopened on 16 March 2026 with a new exhibition; the 45-minute guided coastal auction tour runs Monday to Friday at 16:00.
new.tip: About 15.50 euros adult in holidays; reservations recommended.
new.q: Haliotika, La Cité de la Pêche, Le Guilvinec

new.title: Boat to the Île Vierge lighthouse from the Aber Wrac'h
new.desc: A vedette crosses in about 5 minutes from the Aber Wrac'h to the 82.5 m lighthouse, Europe's tallest, with 365 steps.
new.tip: Boat about 12 euros; check tides.

new.title: Take a surf lesson at La Torche
new.desc: Pointe de la Torche in Plomeur is a surf, windsurf and kitesurf spot with several schools such as Twenty Nine, rooted in 1994.
new.tip: Lessons run all year; powerful waves, take a coach.

new.title: Walk the Bois d'Amour and Trémalo chapel
new.desc: The official Pont-Aven walk starts at the Trémalo chapel, where Gauguin's wooden crucifix inspired The Yellow Christ, and follows the Aven to the Bois d'Amour.
new.tip: Chapel about 10:00 to 17:00; pair with the mills.
new.q: Bois d'Amour and Chapelle de Trémalo, Pont-Aven

new.title: Join the Festival de Cornouaille in Quimper
new.desc: The 103rd edition ran from 23 to 26 July 2026 in the historic centre, with a Grand Défilé and fest-noz.
new.tip: Dates move each July; check the programme.
